title: Magnetoplasmon molecule
authors: A. V. Larionov, A. V. Gorbunov, A. B. Van'kov, D. A. Shchigarev, L. V. Kulik, V. Umansky
abstract: We investigate a two-dimensional electron system in an external magnetic field. An intrinsic four-particle excitation of the electron system, which we term a magnetoplasmon molecule, is observed. The molecule comprises two identical electrons and two Fermi holes with opposite spins. Both electrons and one Fermi hole participate in the collective plasma oscillations of the electron system, whereas the second Fermi hole neutralizes the excess electronic charge. We examine the interaction between the magnetoplasmon molecule and a magnetoexciton condensate.
summary: This paper reports the experimental detection of a 'magnetoplasmon molecule,' a complex four-particle excitation in a 2DES under a magnetic field. Using low-temperature photoluminescence spectroscopy, the authors analyze spectral features and pump-power dependencies to confirm the existence of this bound state. The findings advance the understanding of strongly correlated electron dynamics in quantum Hall systems.
main_problem: The study investigates the formation and properties of a novel intrinsic four-particle excitation, termed a magnetoplasmon molecule, within a two-dimensional electron system subjected to a strong external magnetic field.
main_result: The authors report the experimental observation of this hybrid magnetoplasmon molecule, characterized by specific spectral features and distinct power-law dependencies in the photoluminescence intensity.
method: The research employs spectroscopic measurements (Photoluminescence, PL) on a high-quality GaAs/AlGaAs quantum well, analyzing energy-loss spectra derived from photoexcited carrier recombination.
model_or_system: The physical system is a 2DES in a quantum well under a magnetic field, involving quasi-equilibrium ensembles of Cyclotron Spin-Flip Excitons (CSFEs). The molecule itself is a four-particle complex consisting of two electrons and two Fermi holes.
key_observables: PL spectra showing distinct molecular ($	ext{Mpm}$), plasmaron ($	ext{Pln}$), and trion ($	ext{T}$) features; superlinear/linear dependence of PL intensity on pump power ($I_{	ext{pump}}$); and energy-loss features exceeding single magnetoplasmon energies.
important_parameters: Low temperatures ($T \approx 400-600 	ext{ mK}$); low electron density ($n_e = 2 	imes 10^{11} 	ext{ cm}^{-2}$); and varying excitation spot sizes ($	ext{dpump} \approx 10 	ext{ µm}$ for molecular state observation).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the system operates in the single-excitation limit for certain measurements, and the theoretical description relies on modeling the interaction between the molecule and the CSFE condensate.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate PL spectra showing molecular/plasmaron/trion features, energy-loss spectra comparing calculated DOS to experiment, and PL intensity dependence on pump power, particularly noting the transition from quadratic to linear dependence upon condensate formation.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first establishing the theoretical basis for the hybrid molecule, then detailing the experimental setup and measurement techniques using PL spectroscopy, and finally presenting evidence through power-law analysis and spectral feature identification to confirm the molecule's existence and its interaction with the CSFE condensate.
why_interesting: This work bridges concepts from strongly correlated electron physics (high-density electron systems, excitons) with collective excitations (plasmons), offering experimental validation of complex, multi-particle bound states in quantum Hall systems.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. (a) Calculated quantum-well potential and lowest-subband envelope wave function. (b) PL spectrum at ν = 2 and T = 400 mK, with dpump ≈0.8 mm and Ipump ≈2 mW cm−2; the insets show the plasmaron (Pln) and trion (T) channels. (c) Calculated CSFE and magnetoplasmon dispersions. (d) Energy-loss spectrum of the photoexcited-hole recombination; the red curve is calculated for a Boltzmann CSFE distribution. (e) Spin-selective PL pathways. Recombination of hv with e0 creates hn. In the Pln channel, e and hn form the magnetoplasmon component and qMP = qCSFE; in the T channel, hn and ho occupy the same spin sublevel. Arrows denote optical transitions; positions are schematic.

FIG. 2. PL spectra of the 2DES at T = 600 mK and dpump ≈10 µm. (a,b) Evolution over Ipump ≈0.1–20 W cm−2. (c) Polarization-resolved molecular (Mpm), plasmaron (Pln0, PlnM), and trion (T) features; the upper diagrams show the initial and final configurations. (d) Schematic molecular channel. Recombination of hv creates hn; both excited electrons and hn form the plasma-active component, while ho compensates its charge. The contours indicate constituent grouping, not a calculated geometry.

FIG. 3. (a) Energy-loss spectrum at T = 600 mK, dpump ≈10 µm, and Ipump ≈0.3 W cm−2 (black). The red curve is the two-magnetoplasmon density of states (DOS) at zero total generalized momentum, rescaled by α < 1; the inset shows the initial biexciton dispersion. (b) Momentum-space reference: +q and −q give Q = 0, with E2MP(q) = 2EMP(q). Finite-q stationary points enhance the DOS. The schematic is not a molecular geometry or an assignment of the two molecular lines to separate van Hove features.

FIG. 4. (a) Pump-dependent PL as the CSFE ensemble crosses over from gas to condensate at T = 600 mK and dpump ≈10 µm; Ipump = 0.2, 0.5, 2, and 10 W cm−2 from bottom to top. (b) Single-particle and collective occupation of the CSFE dispersion minimum. (c) Two-CSFE phonon-assisted relaxation from q ≈0 to q ≈1/lB. In the dilute limit, the pair-event rate satisfies Rpair ∝n2 0.

FIG. 5. (a) Integrated PL intensity versus pump power P. (b) PL-channel intensities normalized to the integrated PL; the gray region marks the condensate regime above Pc ≈0.9 µW. (c) Qualitative real-space schematic. The pump spot is fixed, whereas the CSFE region spreads in the condensate. Since ηi = Ii/I0 PL and I0 PL ∝P, ηi ∝P corresponds to Ii ∝P 2, while constant ηi corresponds to Ii ∝P. The spatial profiles are schematic.
